name: Home transcranial electrical stimulation (Flow tDCS, Alpha-Stim and Fisher Wallace CES)
founders: Daniel Månsson (Flow Neuroscience co-founder, clinical psychologist)
Daniel L. Kirsch (Alpha-Stim inventor; founded Electromedical Products International 1981)
Chip Fisher (Fisher Wallace Laboratories co-founder, chairman)
founded_year_range: Alpha-Stim/EPI 1981 (founded by Kirsch; first FDA 510(k) June 1983); Fisher-Wallace Laboratories LLC Dec 2006 (Wikipedia: 2007; current Inc. Aug 2019); Flow Jan 2016 (EU CE mark 2019; FDA PMA P230024 Dec 2025; US launch 1 Sept 2026). Underlying CES/electrosleep dates to the 1950s-60s.
cost_summary: Flow: EUR 459 one-off or EUR 89/month rental in the EU, GBP 399 in the UK; US launch price reported at US$2,200 (ThePrint citing WIRED, Sept 2026) versus the US$500-800 target given at approval (Reuters Dec 2025); prescription-only in US. Halo sister headset ~US$600. Alpha-Stim (US store, Wayback May 2026): AID US$882, M US$1,363; NICE lists AID at GBP 450; HSA/FSA accepted. Fisher Wallace Version 1.0 was US$699 (2015) but has not been sold since April 2023; OAK price not published.
mechanisms: autonomic/nervous system dysregulation (sympathetic overdrive, "stuck in fight-or-flight")
mechanism_summary: No disease theory of their own. The devices assume circuit or oscillatory dysregulation that weak current can normalise. tDCS (Flow) uses 2 mA anodal stimulation of the left DLPFC to raise prefrontal excitability, via LTP-like after-effects, and restore top-down control of limbic circuits in depression. In research, anodal M1 tDCS is used for fibromyalgia and pain, to modulate thalamic and descending inhibition and reduce central sensitization. CES (Alpha-Stim, Fisher Wallace) delivers ear or temple alternating microcurrent. It is claimed to shift EEG toward alpha, lower arousal, and modulate neurotransmitters and the autonomic state. This rests largely on small, industry-linked physiology studies.
techniques: 2 mA anodal left-DLPFC tDCS, 30 min, 5x/week for 3 weeks then 2-3x/week to 10-12 weeks (Flow)
app-guided session scheduling and adherence logging with behaviour-therapy exercises and MADRS-S self-ratings
local microcurrent probes for pain (Alpha-Stim M)
temple-electrode CES headband 20 min 1-2x daily (Fisher Wallace)
M1 anodal tDCS for fibromyalgia (research protocols)
mainstream_notes: Flow FL-100 received FDA PMA (P230024, 8 Dec 2025; supplement S001 Jul 2026), the first home brain stimulation device approved for MDD (adults, moderate-severe, non-treatment-resistant); prescription-only, US launch 1 Sept 2026. Flow reports use in six NHS trusts (company figure). The IFCN guideline (Lefaucheur 2017) gives Level B probable efficacy for tDCS in non-resistant depression, fibromyalgia and craving. In Dec 2019 the FDA reclassified CES for anxiety/insomnia to Class II and required PMA for depression, citing lack of valid evidence. Alpha-Stim is FDA-cleared for anxiety, insomnia and pain only; it has had NHS pilots, NICE (MIB193, then MTG56/HTG570) does not recommend routine adoption for anxiety, and the independent NIHR Alpha-Stim-D trial was null. Fisher Wallace stopped marketing its Version 1.0 device in April 2023; its OAK anxiety 510(k) (submitted Apr 2026) received an FDA additional-information hold in Jun 2026, and it has a VA feasibility study (Birmingham VA, 2026). Cochrane rates the chronic-pain tDCS evidence very low quality. None is routine first-line care.
insurance_notes: Generally out of pocket in the US. Alpha-Stim accepts HSA/FSA and offers military/veteran discounts. Flow said in Dec 2025 that US payer coverage would follow in 2026; no payer coverage had been announced as of Oct 2026 (press: 'still evolving'). Some NHS trusts funded Alpha-Stim and Flow pilots.

key_trials.citation: Woodham RD ... Fu CHY. Nat Med 2025;31:87-95 (epub Oct 2024). PMID 39433921
key_trials.design: Fully remote multisite double-blind sham-controlled phase 2 RCT, Flow headset, 10 weeks, real-time supervised; FDA pivotal (Empower) trial
key_trials.finding: HDRS improvement 9.41 vs 7.14 points (CI of difference 0.51-4.01, p=0.012); response ~58% vs ~38% (secondary; some press mislabelled as remission)

key_trials.citation: Borrione L ... Brunoni AR. JAMA Psychiatry 2024;81:329-337. PMID 38170541
key_trials.design: Three-arm double-blind sham-controlled unsupervised home tDCS (+/- digital therapy) RCT, major depressive episode, Brazil (generic tDCS)
key_trials.finding: No arm superior to sham on HDRS-17 (d -0.25 to 0.05)

key_trials.citation: Morriss R ... Kai J. Lancet Psychiatry 2023;10:172-183. PMID 36724796
key_trials.design: Independent NIHR multicentre double-blind RCT, Alpha-Stim AID (100 uA, 1 h daily, 8 weeks) vs sham, UK primary care depression
key_trials.finding: Negative: GRID-HDRS-17 change at 16 weeks -5.9 vs -6.5 (p=0.46)

key_trials.citation: Brunoni AR et al. N Engl J Med 2017;376:2523-2533. PMID 28657871
key_trials.design: Single-centre double-blind noninferiority RCT (ELECT-TDCS): clinic tDCS 2 mA 30 min vs escitalopram vs placebo, unipolar depression, Brazil (generic tDCS)
key_trials.finding: HDRS-17 decrease 9.0 (tDCS) vs 11.3 (escitalopram) vs 5.8 (placebo); tDCS superior to placebo but not noninferior to escitalopram

key_trials.citation: Barclay TH, Barclay RD. J Affect Disord 2014;164:171-177. PMID 24856571
key_trials.design: Double-blind sham-controlled RCT, Alpha-Stim CES, anxiety disorders with comorbid depression, primary care
key_trials.finding: Active superior for anxiety (d=0.94) and depression (d=0.78); industry-linked

key_trials.citation: McClure D et al. J Nerv Ment Dis 2015;203:827-835. PMID 26414234
key_trials.design: Pilot sham-controlled RCT of CES (Fisher Wallace-type device), bipolar II depression
key_trials.finding: Depression scores improved with active CES; very small sample

key_trials.citation: Caumo W et al. JAMA Netw Open 2025;8:e2514262. PMID 40478572
key_trials.design: Double-blind sham-controlled RCT of home-based tDCS (2 mA, 20 min daily) plus exercise and pain neuroscience education, fibromyalgia, women (generic tDCS, Brazil)
key_trials.finding: Pain interference (MPII) reduced 38.8% vs 16.1% (d=0.73); >=50% improvement 62.5% vs 37.5%

key_trials.citation: Haimi M et al. JMIR Ment Health 2026;13:e92522. PMID 42696738
key_trials.design: Systematic review (12 studies) and meta-analysis of 6 sham-controlled home-tDCS RCTs for MDD
key_trials.finding: g=0.36 (0.06-0.66); not robust to removal of largest positive trial; two largest trials (n=210 unsupervised, n=141 self-administered) negative

key_trials.citation: Shekelle PG et al. Ann Intern Med 2018;168:414-421. PMID 29435567
key_trials.design: Systematic review of 26 CES RCTs (VA ESP)
key_trials.finding: Insufficient evidence for pain, insomnia, depression; low-strength modest benefit in patients with anxiety and depression

key_trials.citation: O'Connell NE et al. Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2018;4:CD008208. PMID 29652088
key_trials.design: Cochrane review of NIBS for chronic pain (tDCS subset 27 studies)
key_trials.finding: tDCS SMD -0.43, very low quality, no disability benefit

key_trials.citation: Teixeira PEP et al. Neuromodulation 2023;26:715-727. PMID 36435660
key_trials.design: Meta-analysis of 16 RCTs of tDCS in fibromyalgia
key_trials.finding: Pain reduction vs sham SMD 1.22 (0.80-1.65); protocols >=4 weeks larger effects; high heterogeneity, limited quality

controversy: The CES evidence is dominated by small, manufacturer-linked trials (e.g., EPI-affiliated meta-analysis authors). The largest independent sham-controlled trial (Alpha-Stim-D for depression, N=236) was null; a reported null remote GAD preprint could not be located. In 2019 the FDA stated there was no valid evidence that CES treats depression. Home tDCS for depression has mixed results: the supervised Flow trial was positive, while the two largest unsupervised/self-administered trials were negative. Critics (Wexler) say the Flow/Halo pairing blurs medical and wellness device lines. Safety concerns include burns from dried or reused pads, DIY montages, and long-term unsupervised use. Fibromyalgia meta-analyses show large effects from small, heterogeneous trials, and Cochrane rates chronic-pain tDCS evidence very low quality. Flow's US price (~US$2,200) is far above its EU price and its own approval-time estimate. Fisher Wallace warned customers that some Version 1.0 devices could overheat if batteries were reversed.

popularity.method_notes: Grouped entry, with the trajectory starting at the Alpha-Stim/EPI founding (1981). Activity levels are judgement-based and anchored on documented events: CES growth in the mid-2000s and the Jan 2011 WSJ feature; the consumer/DIY tDCS boom of 2012-2016; Flow's EU launch in 2019 and growth to >55k users by 2025 and 65k+ by Oct 2026; the Nat Med trial (Oct 2024) and FDA PMA (Dec 2025); Flow US launch (Sept 2026), Fisher Wallace off-market since Apr 2023 with OAK 510(k) on hold in 2026; the rise in home-tDCS publications 2023-2026. User counts are unaudited company claims. Reddit metrics could not be retrieved (Reddit blocks automated access); Google Trends not available programmatically.
